name: Republic of South Africa

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Land area 1,213,090 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2, mid); high is surface area incl. inland water 1,219,602 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 64,747,319). Low allows for census uncertainty; high adds one year of growth to 2026 (~1.2%/yr).

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2025 p.490 as quoted: 69,200 active. CIA Factbook 2025 65-70,000 (low). World Bank MS.MIL.TOTL.P1 89,000 (2020) includes reserves on call-up.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2025 as quoted: 15,050 reserves (Army Reserve regiments). Training levels uneven.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 69,200 (IISS 2025) minus infantry P roles (6,000 + 14,000) = 49,200: Navy ~7,000, Air Force ~10,000, Military Health Service ~8,000, armour/artillery crews, logistics, staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Regional analogy: no conscription since 1994 and a hollowed-out reserve; small volunteer expansion only. Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Mechanised infantry (Ratel/Badger battalions, 7 SA Infantry Bn, 8 SAI) ~ 3-4 battalions plus reserve regiments. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_African_Army)

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: Ratel IFV (1970s) with first Badger IFVs.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: professional volunteers, but budget-limited exercises.

count.note: Educated guess. Motorised, parachute (44 Para) and light infantry battalions; ~2,000 deployed to the DRC until 2025.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: peacekeeping experience; SAMIDRC losses (Goma, Jan 2025).

count.note: Army equipment list: Olifant Mk1B 44 active (mid), Olifant Mk1A 133 mostly in storage; MBT list gives 167 Olifant 1A/1B (high). Low: IISS-type estimates of ~24 operational. Rooikat (242 acquired) excluded as wheeled recce.
Army list: Ratel ~500 active (+~600 stored, parliamentary report Aug 2025) + Badger 22 + Mamba 440+ + Casspir 370+ (Project Sepula note) = ~1,330 active. High adds stored Ratels.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: ageing Ratel, mine-protected Mamba/Casspir (excellent MRAP lineage).

count.note: Army list (acquired): G6 ~153 + G5 ~75 + G4 ~32 + G2 ~75 + G1 ~30 + Bateleur ~25 + Valkiri ~26 = ~416 (high). Mid ~140 assumes about a third active (most G6/G5 in storage per the list).

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: G5/G6 155 mm 45-cal were world-class designs.

count.note: Gripen C 17 + D 9 = 26 (2 Squadron, AFB Makhado). Low: reports of only a handful airworthy for lack of maintenance contracts.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75 minus: Gripen C/D modern 4th-gen with IRIS-T/A-Darter.

count.note: 85 Combat Flying School Hawk Mk.120 24 (lead-in fighter trainers with a light attack role). Low reflects serviceability.
Squadron table: Rooivalk 11 + A109 ~18 (4+5+9) + Oryx (~39 in inventory, number per squadron not given) + BK117 + Super Lynx 4 = ~75; mid 70, low for serviceability.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Rooivalk attack helicopter, Oryx (Puma derivative).

count.note: ATE Vulture 4+ (artillery target acquisition, Group 2); SAAF Seeker II retired. Milkor 380 MALE in development.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: MEKO frigates with Umkhonto and Exocet, ageing.

count.note: Warrior-class MMIPV 3 + Warrior strike craft 1 active (2 in reserve) + River-class MCM up to 4 (status unclear) + Drakensberg replenishment 1 = ~8.
Heroine-class (Type 209/1400) 3 boats; phased refits, typically one or two available.
Battery conversion (SOURCES.md): Oerlikon GDF 35 mm ~169 acquired at ~6 guns per battery ~28, ZU-23-2 Zumlac 36 ~6, Starstreak LML and Umkhonto-GBADS small numbers. Mid ~20 active.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: point defence only, no medium/long-range SAM.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: trained staff system and doctrine heritage (SADF), but budget cuts and the costly 2025 DRC (SAMIDRC) deployment exposed weaknesses.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: professional volunteers; ageing force and integration legacy.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5: average; underfunding and equipment grounding hurt morale.

weapons.note: Anchor 9: G5/G6, Umkhonto, A-Darter, Mokopa, Rooivalk; domestic industry (Denel, Rheinmetall Denel Munition).

ships.note: Anchor 9: MEKO A-200 frigates, Type 209 submarines.

logistics.note: Anchor 9 minus: 1960s C-130BZ, no A400M; decent rail/road network.

communications.note: Anchor 9: data links, satellite comms leased.

isr.note: Anchor 9 minus: no military satellites; small UAV fleet.

cyber.note: Anchor 9: Defence Cyber Command being established.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 704,478,979,350 2011 int$ / population 64,747,319 = 10,880. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 880,048,693,754 x 0.8005 = 704,478,979,350 2011 int$. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 0.74% of GDP in 2025. Lowest share in decades; budget concentrated on personnel.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction (and mining/oil where present) 24.1% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). +/-2 points.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.25 -> 0.95. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ZAF/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 5.41% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 1.00 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.97-1.03). Mid 1 - 0.054/1.00 = 0.95. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.97 = 0.93. High: s 1.03 = 0.95. Net exporter: production is about 100% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Net exporter of maize, fruit and wine; commercial farming sector. Not from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 31,504,125 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share aged 15-19 8.670% / 5 = 546,259. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10%.

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. Denel Land Systems (Badger), Paramount, OTT, DCD Protected Mobility build MRAPs/IFVs mainly for export. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_South_African_Army)

artillery.note: Educated guess. G6/T5 production lines dormant but restartable; Rheinmetall Denel Munition produces shells. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_South_African_Army)

roadKm.note: Road list (2016): 750,000 km total incl. unproclaimed rural roads (high), 158,124 km paved (mid), 1,927 km controlled-access.

railKm.note: asOf 2021: 20,953 route-km (World Bank IS.RRS.TOTL.KM). CIA Factbook 30,400 km (2021) spans the range. Mostly Cape gauge (1,067 mm), heavily electrified; Transnet freight network in decline.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 8 ports, 2 large + 4 medium = 6 (Durban, Cape Town, Richards Bay, Saldanha, Gqeberha, Mossel Bay).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. CIA Factbook: 110 ships under the South African flag (2023), mostly small; not in the DWT list. (context page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/africa/sf.json)

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Long-range wheeled doctrine inherited from the SADF Border War (operations 250+ km into Angola); current sustainment capacity reduced.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, donkeys and mules (not from FAO data); militarily irrelevant.

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces.

chokepoints: Cape of Good Hope sea route

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: familiar terrain, local supply, large cities and population support; no harsh-climate bonus.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data, 2026 order of battle. Counts from the Wikipedia South African Army equipment list (largely "acquired" totals with notes on storage and a 2025 parliamentary report on active Ratels), the SAAF squadron table and the SAN active-ships list; serviceability is the main uncertainty (Gripens and Hawks largely grounded in 2023-24 for lack of support contracts). Population convention: everything inside ne:ZAF. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. ships_major = frigates. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). SAMIDRC deployment to the DRC ended with withdrawal in 2025.
